rich.text: Pri Etz Chaim, Gate of the Sabbath 18

(Kabbalah) — The Arizal's teaching on the three Shabbat meals calls the third meal "an inheritance without boundaries," because at that hour no kelipah holds sway and Ze'ir Anpin rises close to the "supernal brow" of Atika; this meal is tied to the verse "and I will feed you the inheritance of Yaakov your father." Rav Tzadok builds on the same pairing of the third meal, the boundless inheritance and the revelation of Atika.

p: And so too every soul of Israel
the day of Shabbat in observance,
the inheritance of Yaakov your father" —
that holiness will go with him
"that I may dwell in the house of Hashem
all the days of my life," etc.
"On the day that Hashem gives you rest," etc.,
with which you were made to serve."
And it is expounded in the holy Zohar
as referring to the day of Shabbat,
which is "the day of giving rest."
in the midst of the hard labor,
since on the day of Shabbat
the yoke of Torah in truth.

rich.text: (Bereshit) — וְדָא תּוֹסֶפֶת יַהֲבַת לְעַלְמָּא קַדִּישָׁא. וּבְהַהוּא תּוֹסֶפֶת חָדָאן וְיִתְנְשֵׁי מִנַּיְיהוּ כָּל מִלִּין דְּחוֹל וְכָל צַעֲרִין וְכָל עָאקִין כְּמָא דְאַתְּ אָמֵר בְּיוֹם הָנִיחַ יְיָ לְךָ מֵעָצְבְּךָ וּמֵרָגְזֶךָ וּמִן הָעֲבֹדָה הַקָּשָׁה — "This addition [of soul] she gives to the holy people; with it they rejoice and forget all weekday matters, all sorrows and troubles, as it says, 'on the day Hashem gives you rest ...'" The paragraph runs from the end of 48a onto 48b; the words Rav Tzadok relies on stand right after the start of 48b, as he says (רֵישׁ עַמּוּד ב).
